purpose.content: Aster introduces a new remote monitoring capability for a greenhouse that previously used manual readings. The goal is continuous visibility, not a narrow change to an existing interface.

fields.system_boundary: The capability includes local sensing, buffering, and remote reading; irrigation control and long-term analytics are separate systems.

requirements.content: The capability shall sample once per minute, retain the latest ten valid readings during connectivity loss, and expose current and recent values to an authorized controller.

fields.normative_statements: Provide 60-second sampling, UTC timestamps, ten-reading outage history, latest-reading queries, and explicit invalid-data rejection.
fields.rationale: Operators need trustworthy current conditions and a small outage history without turning the hub into a control or analytics platform.

acceptance.content: Capability acceptance combines a scheduled sampling demonstration, an outage demonstration, and an authorized-query demonstration with measurable outputs.

fields.measurable_conditions: Sixty valid readings arrive in one hour, the newest ten survive a 20-minute outage, and an authorized controller retrieves the expected latest value.
fields.verification_method: Demonstrate with fake time, a scripted probe, an outage switch, and an authorized test controller; this example does not execute the demonstrations.

trace.content: The new capability decomposes into context, composition, interaction, data, operation, and verification artifacts rather than duplicating those details here.

fields.model_elements: Example::Sensor, Example::Controller, and Example::WeatherService identify the new capability's participants.
fields.design_links: Aster system-context and reading-pipeline designs own realization; the requirements retain only their observable goals and constraints.

limits.content: Enrollment, authorization mechanics, multi-year retention, and actuator safety requirements need separate analysis before a real capability is approved.

fields.unresolved_items: Controller enrollment, credential management, long-term storage, and actuator safety are outside this worked capability example.

boundary.content:
AsterHub is the only element inside the product boundary. Operator and WeatherService are external actors; the figure shows exchange direction without implying internal decomposition.

fields.system_boundary: AsterHub owns sampling and buffering; Operator and WeatherService, probe power supply, and irrigation decisions are outside.
fields.external_actors: Operator requests current readings and sends calibration commands; WeatherService supplies forecast data used only for display context.
fields.diagram_decisions: [{"concern":"system-boundary","applies":true,"choice":"figure","rationale":"A boundary view makes inside/outside ownership and exchange direction unambiguous.","asset":"assets/system-context.svg","model_view":"Example::SystemContext"}]

interfaces.content: Validated readings leave AsterHub for Operator, calibration commands enter from Operator, and forecast records arrive from WeatherService without being stored as sensor measurements.

fields.information_flows: Outgoing Reading and HistoryResponse, incoming CalibrationCommand, and incoming ForecastRecord have distinct meanings and owners.
fields.interface_participants: AsterHub is provider for readings and receiver for calibration; Operator consumes readings; WeatherService is a read-only forecast source.

behavior.content: AsterHub continues sampling when Operator disconnects and labels forecast data as external context rather than using it to alter readings.

fields.interactions: Operator queries and calibrates, WeatherService publishes forecasts, and AsterHub samples and responds independently of forecast availability.
fields.states: Online, operator-disconnected, and forecast-unavailable states clarify which external losses do and do not affect collection.

constraints.content: No external actor may rewrite buffered history, and calibration commands never change the meaning of the Reading timestamp or measured value.

fields.constraints: History is read-only externally, forecast data is informational, and calibration applies only to subsequent samples.
fields.design_rationale: These boundaries prevent external systems from silently corrupting measurement provenance or becoming hidden sampling dependencies.

trace.content: Example::SystemContext names the fictional view behind the figure; the component-composition and operation-contract examples own internal and protocol details.

fields.model_elements: Example::SystemContext, Example::Sensor, Example::Controller, and Example::WeatherService define the context participants and view.
fields.verification_links: A planned context review checks boundary placement, actor coverage, exchange direction, and the absence of internal-only details.

metadata.title: Aster collector buffer and exporter composition

context.content: Within the AsterHub boundary, three components divide acquisition, retention, and query work; external actors are intentionally omitted from this composition view.

fields.system_boundary: Only Collector, RingBuffer, and Exporter are internal components in this example.
fields.external_actors: Probe and Operator appear only as interface endpoints so component responsibilities remain clear.

parts.content: Collector validates and timestamps, RingBuffer keeps ten valid readings, and Exporter answers queries without mutation. A table is sufficient for these three responsibilities.

fields.parts: Collector, UtcClock, RingBuffer, and Exporter are the purposeful parts; no further decomposition is needed.
fields.responsibilities: Collector rejects invalid values, clock supplies UTC, buffer evicts oldest-first, and exporter returns newest or NOT_READY.
fields.diagram_decisions: [{"concern":"component-structure","applies":true,"choice":"table","rationale":"Three responsibilities and two relationships are clearer in a table than another diagram.","asset":null,"model_view":null}]

relationships.content: Collector depends on UtcClock and writes RingBuffer; Exporter depends only on RingBuffer's read interface and cannot call append or evict.

fields.relationships: Collector→UtcClock for time, Collector→RingBuffer for append, and Exporter→RingBuffer for readLatest are the only internal dependencies.
fields.interfaces: RingBuffer exposes append(Reading) to Collector and readLatest() to Exporter; mutation is unavailable to Exporter.

behavior.content: The collector continues appending while the exporter is unavailable, and the eleventh valid sample evicts only the oldest retained sample.

fields.interactions: Validation precedes append, readLatest returns a copy, and export failure never propagates back into collection.
fields.states: Empty, partially full, and full buffer states distinguish NOT_READY, append, and FIFO eviction behavior.

constraints.content: The composition intentionally avoids a shared database or bidirectional controller dependency so each internal responsibility remains independently testable.

fields.constraints: One writer per buffer, read-only export, ten-entry capacity, and no controller callback into collection.
fields.design_rationale: Single-writer FIFO and narrow interfaces make ordering, ownership, and failure isolation easy to inspect.

trace.content: The composition traces to Example::Sensor and the interaction design; buffer eviction and exporter-isolation checks cover the important relationships.

fields.model_elements: Example::Sensor provides the owning part; Collector, RingBuffer, and Exporter are language-side design responsibilities.
fields.verification_links: Planned capacity, read-only export, FIFO eviction, and controller-outage cases verify composition behavior.

purpose.content: The design explains the ordering for one current-reading request, including validation and timeout behavior rather than static schema details.

fields.design_subject: Synchronous request/validation/response flow between Controller and Sensor with one timeout alternate.
fields.requirements_links: Latest-reading query, explicit invalid-input rejection, and no-fabricated-value requirements drive the flow.

participants.content: Controller originates ReadRequest, Sensor checks sensorId and buffer state, and the operation boundary returns ReadingResponse or an explicit outcome.

fields.participants: Controller is the requester; Sensor is the provider; RingBuffer is an internal read-only participant, not an external actor.
fields.interfaces: ReadRequest carries sensorId; ReadingResponse carries Reading, NOT_READY, UNKNOWN_SENSOR, or TIMEOUT.

flow.content:
The numbered flow is request, validation, buffer read, then response; timeout cannot produce a ReadingResponse after the deadline.

![Aster request and response ordering](assets/interaction-flow.svg)

> **Figure D102-1 — Aster request and response ordering.**  
> **Question:** In what order do request, validation, response, and timeout occur?  
> **Model view:** Example::InteractionFlow  
> **Companions:** The operation-contract and alternate-flow tables.  
> **Status:** renderable-now; designed-only  
> **Reading:** Controller sends ReadRequest, Sensor validates the request, then returns ReadingResponse; the dashed timeout path returns no reading.  
> **Limits:** The view is fictional and omits transport encoding, authentication, and precise timeout duration.

fields.interactions: Controller sends ReadRequest, Sensor validates sensorId, reads newest valid Reading, and sends ReadingResponse.
fields.ordering: Validation precedes buffer access, buffer access precedes response, and timeout terminates the attempt without a value response.
fields.diagram_decisions: [{"concern":"interaction-ordering","applies":true,"choice":"figure","rationale":"Numbered arrows and lifelines make request, validation, response, and timeout order explicit.","asset":"assets/interaction-flow.svg","model_view":"Example::InteractionFlow"}]

alternates.content: Unknown sensorId returns UNKNOWN_SENSOR before buffer access, empty history returns NOT_READY, and timeout produces no reading rather than a stale fabricated response.

fields.alternate_flows: UNKNOWN_SENSOR skips reading, NOT_READY follows an empty read, and TIMEOUT ends the operation without ReadingResponse.
fields.error_behavior: Errors are explicit outcomes and never mutate history or turn an old value into a newly timestamped reading.

constraints.content: The flow is read-only and single-request; concurrent retries, authentication, and transport retransmission are deliberately outside this example.

fields.behavior: One request produces at most one terminal outcome and never changes buffer contents or reading timestamps.
fields.constraints: No response after timeout, no buffer mutation, and no implicit retry or fallback value.

projection.content: Tests record event order for success, unknown sensor, empty history, and timeout paths and inspect the corresponding Example::InteractionFlow view.

fields.source_projection: RequestHandler, RequestValidator, ReadLatestExporter, and a controllable timeout are intended design units.
fields.verification_links: Ordered success, unknown-sensor, empty-history, and timeout event-sequence cases are planned checks.

purpose.content: getCurrentReading returns the newest valid value for one known sensor without exposing history mutation or acting as a generic data schema.

fields.boundary: The operation is the public query boundary; validation, buffering, and controller orchestration remain internal or external respectively.
fields.participants: Controller invokes the operation and Aster export adapter executes it read-only.

operation.content: The request contains only sensorId; success returns the current Reading and does not accept time ranges, writes, or arbitrary buffer indices.

fields.operations: getCurrentReading(sensorId) returns Reading, NOT_READY, UNKNOWN_SENSOR, or TIMEOUT and has no retry or mutation side effect.
fields.data_shapes: Request is {sensorId: string}; Reading is {sensorId, utcTimestamp, celsius, quality?} with finite numeric celsius.

errors.content: Unknown identifiers return UNKNOWN_SENSOR before buffer access, empty history returns NOT_READY, and timeout returns no value or fallback timestamp.

fields.error_behavior: UNKNOWN_SENSOR, NOT_READY, and TIMEOUT are terminal outcomes; none creates, updates, or backdates a Reading.
fields.invariants: At most one terminal outcome per request, no history mutation, and success always returns the newest valid value at read time.

compatibility.content: Version 1 returns three required fields; version 2 may add optional quality while preserving request shape, operation name, and all error meanings.

fields.version_policy: Major changes alter required fields or outcomes; optional response fields and additive documentation are minor compatible changes.
fields.compatibility_policy: Old callers may ignore quality and new callers must accept its absence; UNKNOWN_SENSOR and NOT_READY never change meaning.

trace.content: The operation traces to Example::InteractionFlow and planned success, unknown, empty, timeout, and compatibility checks.

fields.model_elements: Example::InteractionFlow defines the fictional request/validation/response order exercised by the operation.
fields.verification_links: Success, unknown, empty, timeout, no-mutation, and version 1/2 response checks are planned verification cases.

metadata.title: Aster outage and cadence test plan

scope.content: The plan tests 60-second cadence and latest-valid behavior during a controller outage; it does not record an executed result or substitute review for execution.

fields.requirements_links: The cadence and latest-valid requirements define observable acceptance for these planned cases.
fields.design_links: Collector, RingBuffer, Exporter, and fake-clock interfaces identify the units under test.

methods.content: Deterministic demonstration drives twelve samples and a two-minute outage while recording every accepted value and exported response.

fields.methods: Use a scheduled demonstration, FIFO boundary analysis, and exact output comparison rather than inspection alone.
fields.environment: Use fake UTC time, an in-memory buffer, a scripted valid probe, and a controllable controller-connection flag.

cases.content: The main case collects twelve valid values, drops the controller after the tenth, and checks collection and export before, during, and after the outage.

fields.inputs: Twelve values 20.0–21.1 Celsius at 60-second ticks, outage after value 20.9, and a final query after value 21.1.
fields.procedure: Record cadence and buffer after each tick, verify controller failure does not stop collection, then query after the twelfth sample.
fields.expected_results: Twelve timestamps are 60 seconds apart, the buffer holds 20.2–21.1, and final export returns 21.1 with its exact UTC timestamp.

criteria.content: Pass requires exact cadence, exact retained values and order, no export during outage, and exact latest-valid response after recovery; all remain planned expectations.

fields.pass_criteria: No missed tick, ten retained values are exactly 20.2–21.1, outage exports are suppressed, and recovery returns only 21.1.
fields.trace_matrix: Cadence maps to tick records, FIFO to retained history, latest-valid to recovery response, and read-only export to unchanged timestamps.

limits.content: The plan does not measure real scheduler jitter, physical sensor accuracy, network behavior, or multi-controller concurrency.

fields.unexecuted_cases: Every case is unexecuted in this fictional document; no transcript or observed outcome is asserted.
fields.residual_risks: Deterministic simulation cannot demonstrate embedded timing, hardware faults, transport security, or production load behavior.
